words.name: click

words.name: confidence

words.name: one-click-hide
words.description: Feature that hides a contribution via a single reversible click

words.name: throttling
words.description: ignoring or limiting the user instead of implementing

words.name: value
words.description: a stored number; reference the provenance qualifier triple, not this bare word

values.description: Assumption: PR is mergeable and reversible; real cost includes review, UX, abuse vetting
Claude's estimate; revisable upward given the open-source PR, since building is no longer the most expensive option
Competing cheaper reaction; Moos supplies the justification for it free of charge
Timon's own estimate: very high failure probability per single attempt, hence a portfolio is required
Father-son transmission nominally raises this to 2 but remains structurally a single point of failure until an external collaborator joins

triples.name: implementation cost
triples.description: Effort for publishers, given an open-source PR is supplied by Timon

triples.name: Annoyance Test Republik
triples.description: Tactic: deliberately irritate the publishers to trigger an open-source implementation of one-click-hide

triples.name: Plato Goal
triples.description: Transmission of the idea to the next generation as the actual addressee, not majority persuasion

triples.name: P(publishers implement | annoyed)
triples.description: Probability that publishers enable the feature in response to irritation, i.e. under the annoyed condition

triples.name: P(publishers throttle | annoyed)
triples.description: Probability of the competing cheaper reaction under the annoyed condition: ignore or limit the user

triples.name: Single-Attempt Failure Rate
triples.description: Share of individual tactics in a portfolio that fail on their own

triples.name: Bus Factor zukunft.com
triples.description: Number of people whose loss would halt the project

triples.name: confidence value
triples.description: The p-value of an assumed value: the subjective probability between 0 and 1 that the tagged estimate is right.
